Hi, this message appears because this AppImage works with fuse3

Are you using gentoo? You might be affected by a bug in the new runtime. 

[There is actually a fix in the works](https://github.com/AppImage/type2-runtime/pull/32), but it is taking a while for it to be merged.

iirc the problem is that on gentoo `/usr/bin/fusermount` doesn't have read permission for the user. Which the new runtime needs.

So the only thing you can do in the meantime is to change the permissions of `/usr/bin/fusermount` so that it can be read by the user.

This other trick might work in the meantime, if it works you don't have to be messing with `/usr/bin/fusermount`

`FUSERMOUNT_PROG=$(which fusermount) ./Steam-1.0.0.79-2-x86_86.AppImage`

`FUSERMOUNT_PROG` can be defined in your bash_profile or zprofile, etc btw.


Edit: Btw you might want to re-download the appimage as there has been some fixes.

Hello everyone, I found the issue.  libappimage by itself does not support `zstd` compressed images, at least not by default,

`
Squashfs image uses (null) compression, this version supports only xz, zlib.
ERROR: appimage_read_file_into_buffer_following_symlinks : sqfs_open_image error: /home/phil/Applications/Steam-1.0.0.81-2-3-x86_64.appimage
`

The solution is to, 1) activate fusefs support in the libappimage build, and
2) for sys-fs/squashfuse, activate support for zstd.

I think this uses more resources than just using libappimage's default xz compression, since Arch's libappimage goes through fuse, but it works now.

- `NVIDIA_HANDLER` is the variable used by Conty to handle Nvidia drivers, value 0 it is disabled, 1 downloads the drivers. The release of Conty we are using is an old one, so it does not have a value 2 that acts instead as follow.
- `NVIDIA_ON` is a variable I use in all Archimages, and also here. It acts like thye new value 2 in newer versions of Conty, it copies drivers from the host into a ~/.local/share/Conty directory from the host system instead of downloading them. Value 0 prevents the use of this method, while value 1 allows copy of drivers locally and exporting the local libraries path to LD_LIBRARY_PATH

to made Conty acting normally you need to:
- set `NVIDIA_HANDLER` to 1
- set `NVIDIA_ON` to 0

In this moment, `NVIDIA_ON` is 1, and exports local libraries, while `NVIDIA_HANDLER` is 0 to be disabled.

Try setting `cachesize=1G` for the FUSE driver.

The main issue here is that steam reads most of the data in the image upon startup and due to the `-B32` that data is scattered across a lot of blocks. At `-S25`, only 16 of these blocks fit in the cache. Once a block gets evicted from the cache, it needs to be decompressed again the next time it's accessed. If you're optimizing for speed, it's good to check the output of the FUSE driver using `debuglevel=verbose` where after unmounting it will print statistics. For the default cache size, you'll see something like:

```
V 07:43:08.752180 blocks created: 174
V 07:43:08.752191 blocks evicted: 154
```

Running *the same image* with `cachesize=1G` will show:

```
V 07:42:16.226506 blocks created: 43
V 07:42:16.226520 blocks evicted: 0
```

If you combine that with proper settings for tidying (e.g. `tidy_strategy=time,tidy_interval=5s,tidy_max_age=10s`), the cache will be fully tidied once the application has started.

Oh, the difference in startup time:

- Default cache size: 11.12s
- 1 GiB cache size: 6.33s

```
mkdir -p ~/.local/lib ~/.local/share/vulkan/implicit_layer.d
cp /usr/lib/libVkLayer_obs_vkcapture.so ~/.local/lib
cp /usr/share/vulkan/implicit_layer.d/obs_vkcapture_64.json ~/.local/share/vulkan/implicit_layer.d
```

then edit `~/.local/share/vulkan/implicit_layer.d/obs_vkcapture_64.json ` and change `library_path` to include the full path to `~/.local/lib/ibVkLayer_obs_vkcapture.so`
